Set the xtra gtsummary theme

Source: R/theme-gtsummary-xtra.R
theme_gtsummary_xtra.Rd

Applies a custom gtsummary theme tailored for publication-ready tables.

Usage

theme_gtsummary_xtra(set_theme = TRUE)

Arguments

set_theme

Logical indicating whether to set the theme via gtsummary::set_gtsummary_theme(). Default is TRUE. When FALSE, the named list of theme elements is returned invisibly without activating the theme.

Value

A named list of gtsummary theme elements (returned invisibly).

Details

The theme configures the following defaults:

  • Package-wide:

    • Sets the theme name to "xtra".

    • Rounds large p-values to 2 decimal places via gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2).

    • Automatically bolds variable labels before conversion with gtsummary::bold_labels(). Because this rule is placed before any table-specific formatting instructions, it can be overridden in a pipeline with gtsummary::remove_bold().

  • Flextable output (gtsummary::as_flex_table()):

    • Disables repeating header rows across page breaks in Word documents (opts_word = list(repeat_headers = FALSE)).

  • Summary tables (gtsummary::tbl_summary()):

    • Disables automatic conversion of numeric variables with few unique values to categorical ("assign_summary_type-arg:cat_threshold" = 0L), so numeric scores remain continuous unless explicitly typed otherwise.

    • Displays all levels of dichotomous variables (all_dichotomous() ~ "categorical").

    • Summarizes continuous variables with "{mean} ({sd})" (rounded to 1 decimal place) and categorical variables with "{n} ({p}%)" (counts as integers and percentages rounded to 1 decimal place).

    • Sets default continuous tests in gtsummary::add_p() to t-test ("t.test" / "svy.t.test") and one-way ANOVA ("oneway.test"), matching gtsummary::theme_gtsummary_mean_sd().

  • Regression and difference tables:

    • In gtsummary::tbl_regression() and gtsummary::tbl_uvregression(), rounds regression coefficients and confidence interval bounds to 2 decimal places via gtsummary::label_style_number(digits = 2).

    • In gtsummary::tbl_regression(), gtsummary::tbl_uvregression(), and gtsummary::add_difference(), merges the estimate and confidence interval columns into a single column formatted as "{estimate} ({conf.low}, {conf.high})" and updates the column header accordingly.

Use gtsummary::reset_gtsummary_theme() to restore the default settings.

See also

gtsummary::theme_gtsummary, gtsummary::set_gtsummary_theme(), gtsummary::reset_gtsummary_theme()

Examples

theme_gtsummary_xtra()
#> Setting theme "xtra"

gtsummary::tbl_summary(
  gtsummary::trial,
  by = "trt",
  include = c("age", "grade", "response")
) |>
  gtsummary::as_flex_table()
